(1) Model still exists and is not superseded in its hardware class: the official QwenLM README (raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.8/main/README.md; the QwenLM/Qwen3.6 repo now redirects to QwenLM/Qwen3.8) dates Qwen3.6-35B-A3B to 2026-04-16 and lists the Qwen3.8 open releases as 2.4T-A95B (2026-08-12) and 27B dense (2026-08-14). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (llama.cpp arch 'qwen4exp', merged PR #27742, 2026-08-27) is a 177B MoE (93.7 GiB at Q4_0 per PR #29887; discussion #30282) and cannot fit 12 GB + 32 GB. No Qwen3.8-35B-A3B was found, and llama.cpp issue #31072 (2026-10-24) states Qwen4 weights are not yet published. So Qwen3.6-35B-A3B remains the current pick for this tier.

(2) Flags are still valid, not deprecated: tools/server/README.md and common/arg.cpp on master document `-ncmoe/--n-cpu-moe`, `-ngl`, `-np`, `-ctk/-ctv q8_0` with no deprecation. BUT defaults have changed: `-ngl` defaults to 'auto', `-np` to -1 (auto) and `--fit` is ON by default, so `-ngl 99` hand-tuning is now optional; the server default port moved from 8080 to 9931 (v0.7.0 notes).

(3) The recipe is no longer the best-known method, which is why the claim is outdated as guidance: llama.cpp PR #29887 (merged 2026-10-07; shipped in v0.7.0 on 2026-10-15, release notes: 'up to 2.2x faster decode when experts are offloaded') added `--moe-cache-mib`, a GPU SLRU cache for CPU-resident experts (PR #30637 merged 2026-10-19). PR #30966 (opened 2026-10-22, still open, adds cpu-share + tuning script) reports Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K_XL on an RTX 2080 Ti 11GB going 42.11 -> 64.5 tok/s and on an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB 44.23 -> 61.1 tok/s, and a mixed setup including an RTX 3060 12GB reaching ~45 t/s. Additionally, built-in MTP and community DSpark drafters (`--spec-type draft-mtp|draft-dspark`, discussions #26230 and #30777, 2026-10-18) give 77-89 tok/s (MTP) and ~100 tok/s on code (DSpark) for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M with `--n-cpu-moe 32` on an 11 GB card.

(4) The plain-recipe numbers themselves are plausible: the 42-44 tok/s 'no cache' baselines above on 11-16 GB cards bracket the claimed 39-47 tok/s, and llama.cpp issue #25859 documents the exact hardware (RTX 3060 12GB, Ryzen 5600X, 32GB DDR4) running Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M with `-ncmoe 26` at ~1143 tok/s prefill, while also showing that single-GPU `-ncmoe` prefill is PCIe-bound (GPU ~42% idle) and that issue is still open as of Oct 2026. Long context is plausible: discussion #28584 shows 354K context on a 16 GB card and `-ngl 99 --n-cpu-moe 17` holding 128K f16 KV in ~15.9 GiB.

Verdict: the model choice and flags are still current, but the claim presents a superseded method and an understated performance ceiling (expert GPU cache and speculative decoding shipped in Oct 2026 push the same model on 11-16 GB cards to ~60-100 tok/s), and its cited sources could not be opened. Confidence is medium because the primary source was unreachable and no isolated 12GB-only before/after for `--moe-cache-mib` alone was found.

KV-cache cost on this card (fp16 K+V, per-token = 2 x n_full_attn_layers x n_kv_heads x head_dim x 2 bytes): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B has 10 softmax-attention layers with 2 KV heads x 256 dim = 20 KiB/token (~0.3 GiB at 16k, ~0.6 GiB at 32k; GDN layers add a fixed ~30 MiB/seq); Qwen3.5-9B ~8 full-attn layers x 4 KV heads x 256 = ~32 KiB/token (~0.5 GiB at 16k, ~1.0 GiB at 32k, inferred from library defaults); Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B is full GQA 48 layers x 4 KV x 128 = 96 KiB/token (1.5 GiB at 16k, 3 GiB at 32k); Devstral Small 2 (40 layers x 8 KV x 128) = 160 KiB/token (2.5/5 GiB); Gemma 4 uses a 1024-token sliding window on 5 of every 6 layers so KV grows slowly past 8k (SWA removes ~70-83% of KV). Resulting 32k-context VRAM estimates at Q4: Qwen3.5-9B ~7-8GB fits; Gemma 4 12B ~9-10GB fits; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B ~10-11GB on GPU with experts in RAM fits (q8 KV halves this); gpt-oss-20b ~13.5GB does not fully fit; Qwen3-Coder-30B/GLM-4.7-Flash/Nemotron ~20-22GB need expert offload; Qwen3.6-27B/Qwen3.8-27B/Devstral Small 2 18-21GB dense do not fit.

unverified_beyond_cap: LiteLLM proxy (~62k stars, PyPI 1.106.3 on 2026-10-24) serves both OpenAI-format /v1/chat/completions and an Anthropic-format /messages endpoint across providers, so a single proxy can front Ollama and Anthropic for OpenAI-compatible frontends (OpenCode, Cline, Zed, Open WebUI, Qwen Code, Aider) and in principle for Anthropic-format clients; it is installed with `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`.

Ollama's native Anthropic Messages API compatibility (`/v1/messages`) was introduced in Ollama v0.14.0 (GitHub release dated 10 Jan; year 2026 per release ordering and Ollama's 16 Jan 2026 blog post 'Claude Code with Anthropic API compatibility').

Exact Claude Code -> local Ollama configuration: `export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama` (required but ignored), `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""`, `export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434`, then `claude --model <ollama-model>`; or `ollama launch claude [--model <name>] [--yes] [-- <claude args>]`. For Ollama Cloud: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://ollama.com`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$OLLAMA_API_KEY"` (cloud endpoint 'does not accept x-api-key alone'). The local server does not validate the key.

Ollama's /v1/messages supports: messages, streaming, system prompts, multi-turn, base64 vision, tools incl. tool_result, thinking blocks (budget_tokens accepted but not enforced), and request fields model/max_tokens/messages/system/stream/temperature/top_p/top_k/stop_sequences/tools/thinking/output_config(effort). NOT supported: `tool_choice`, `metadata`, `/v1/messages/count_tokens`, prompt caching, Batches, citations, PDF documents, SSE `error` events during streaming. Requires `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` on the hosted endpoint. Any local model name works; to serve Anthropic names (so Claude Code's `haiku` alias hits a local model) use `ollama cp <local> claude-haiku-5-5`.

Claude Code treats any `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` endpoint as the Anthropic API and sends the full feature set: `thinking: {type: adaptive}` (also for unrecognized model IDs), `output_config.effort`, `context_management`, beta tool fields (`strict`, `defer_loading`), and `role: "system"` entries inside `messages` for unrecognized IDs. It auto-retries once without the rejected piece on recognizable 400s (thinking type, system-in-messages, cache_control, effort, context_management, advisor tool). `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1` strips most pre-release fields (but not adaptive thinking, effort, or system-in-messages). Inference posts to `/v1/messages?beta=true`; a `HEAD /api/hello` probe can be rejected harmlessly.

For an unrecognized (non-`claude-`) model ID Claude Code assumes a 200K context window and a 32,000 default / 128,000 cap on output tokens; set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=<n>` (applies directly to IDs not starting with `claude-` and without `[1m]`) and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` to match the local model's num_ctx, otherwise auto-compaction fires at the wrong point or the local model silently truncates. `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` is clamped to >=100,000.

Model-selection env vars: `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` (this session; overrides the `model` setting; `--model`/`/model` override it), `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL` (default for new sessions, v2.1.236+), `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`/`_SONNET_MODEL`/`_HAIKU_MODEL`/`_FABLE_MODEL` (what the alias resolves to; HAIKU also drives background functionality), `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` (default for subagents, teammates and workflow agents; alias or full ID) plus `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (v2.1.257+, ignores frontmatter `model`). `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` is DEPRECATED in favor of `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`. `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION` adds an unvalidated custom entry to `/model` ('you can use any string your API endpoint accepts'). The `_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` variables have no effect behind an ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway.

Behind an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateway with `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` set, background tasks (session titles, summaries, prompt-hook evaluation) run on the MAIN model unless `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` pins one; with an Anthropic Console `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and no AUTH_TOKEN they use the default Haiku model.

Subagent `model` frontmatter accepts an alias (`sonnet`,`opus`,`haiku`,`fable`), `inherit`, or 'a full model ID ... Accepts the same values as the --model flag'. Resolution order: per-invocation model param -> frontmatter -> CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL -> main model. The docs never state that a non-Claude string (e.g. `qwen3-coder`) is accepted in frontmatter, and ALL requests from one Claude Code process go to the single configured base URL, so a subagent cannot be pointed at Ollama while the main agent uses api.anthropic.com without an intermediate proxy that routes by model name.

Claude Code (v2.1.273+) can send gateway hint headers a proxy can route on: `x-claude-code-request-class` (main | subagent | workflow | compaction | auxiliary), `x-claude-code-agent-type` (Explore/Plan/general-purpose/custom/teammate/fork), `x-claude-code-session-id`, `x-claude-code-agent-id`, `x-claude-code-prompt-id`. They are OFF by default for a custom base URL; enable with `CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1`. Values never include prompt text.

Subscription economics: while `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `apiKeyHelper` is active, 'requests carry that credential in place of a developer's claude.ai subscription login, and the subscription's usage limits don't apply' (billed per token to the credential owner). Setting ONLY `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` keeps the saved claude.ai login as the credential, and a pass-through gateway must forward the OAuth capability in `anthropic-beta` or requests 401. Anthropic's terms: OAuth 'is intended exclusively for purchasers of ... subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications'; developers 'may not ... route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users' and 'may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens'. Remote Control is disabled when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is not api.anthropic.com.

Current model IDs/aliases per Claude Code docs (Anthropic API): `opus` -> Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, v2.1.280+), `sonnet` -> Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, v2.1.284+), `haiku` -> Haiku 5.5 (v2.1.293+), `fable` -> Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`). The task brief listed `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` as current Haiku; the docs show Haiku 5.5 now exists and is the `haiku` alias target (the bundled claude-api skill lists `claude-haiku-5-5` at $0.10/$0.50 per MTok, vs Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10). Repo references `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-5` are stale.

Subagent definition contract: files in `.claude/agents/*.md` (project), `~/.claude/agents/` (user), plugin `agents/`, or `--agents '<json>'`; frontmatter `name`, `description` (required), `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`, `permissionMode` (default|acceptEdits|auto|dontAsk|bypassPermissions|plan), `skills` (preloaded), `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `memory` (user|project|local), `maxTurns`, `background`, `isolation: worktree`, `effort`, `autoCompactWindow`, `color`. Limits: 20 concurrent (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`), nesting depth 3, combined descriptions warn above 15,000 tokens. Run a whole session as an agent with `claude --agent <name>` or `"agent": "<name>"` in settings. Subagents start with fresh context; background subagents keep only a fixed built-in tool subset.

Hooks: events include SessionStart, Setup, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Notification, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, Stop, StopFailure, PreCompact, PostCompact, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch, ConfigChange, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate/Remove, Elicitation. Handler types: `command`, `prompt` (one LLM call on the background model, returns {ok, reason, impossible}), `agent` (experimental multi-turn subagent, up to 50 turns), `http`, `mcp_tool`; fields `matcher`, `if`, `timeout`, `async`, `model`, `continueOnBlock`. Exit 2 blocks; JSON `decision: block`/`permissionDecision`/`updatedInput`/`additionalContext`/`continue`. Stop hooks get `stop_hook_active`, `last_assistant_message`, `background_tasks`; 8-consecutive-continuation cap (`CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`). SubagentStop gets `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `agent_transcript_path`. SessionStart can inject `additionalContext` and persist env via `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`. Hooks live in settings.json (user/project/local/managed), plugin hooks.json, and skill/agent frontmatter.

LiteLLM proxy exposes the Anthropic Messages format at `/v1/messages` for any provider in its `model_list` (incl. `ollama/...`), and its official Claude Code guide uses `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<LiteLLM virtual or master key>`, optionally `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=<model_name from config>`; Anthropic's own costs page notes 'Several large enterprises reported using LiteLLM' but that it 'is unaffiliated with Anthropic and has not been audited for security'. docs.litellm.ai and raw GitHub paths were unreachable from this sandbox, so config.yaml syntax was not verified first-hand; a third-party blog alleges two LiteLLM releases (1.82.7/1.82.8) shipped malicious code (unverified).

LiteLLM's `ollama_chat/` provider forwards OpenAI `tools` natively to Ollama /api/chat and maps Ollama `tool_calls` back with finish_reason `tool_calls` (including streaming), whereas the `ollama/` provider (/api/generate) does not list `tools` among its supported OpenAI params.

LiteLLM proxy serves a native Anthropic-format `POST /v1/messages` and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`; for providers without a native Anthropic-messages config (e.g. Ollama) it bridges through `LiteLLMMessagesToCompletionTransformationHandler` -> `litellm.acompletion(**kwargs)` with `tools` carried through, so Claude Code / Anthropic SDK clients can call local models with tool use.

A proxy `CustomLogger.async_pre_call_hook(user_api_key_dict, cache, data, call_type)` may return a modified dict, which the proxy substitutes for the request data before routing (so it can rewrite `data["model"]`), return a str to reject with a message, or raise.

LiteLLM ships a built-in `auto_router/complexity_router` deployment type: rule-based 7-dimension scoring (<1 ms, offline) into SIMPLE/MEDIUM/COMPLEX/REASONING tiers mapped to model groups; classifier_type options heuristic | heuristic_v2 | llm | heuristic_first | hybrid | capability | oss_classifier | custom (ClassifierPlugin); plus keyword_tier_rules, escalation_keywords, plan_mode_min_tier, session_affinity(_ttl_seconds), enable_context_window_escalation(+buffer), stall_escalation_enabled/window/repeat_threshold, modality_routing, route_housekeeping_to_cheapest_tier, tier_labels/tier_definitions, and `plugins` (RoutingPlugin dotted paths).

Virtual keys, per-key/team budgets and spend tracking in the LiteLLM proxy require DATABASE_URL (Postgres); without a DB the proxy runs with master_key only, budgets are not enforced, and router-level provider budgets rely on Redis. Logging callbacks (Langfuse, langfuse_otel, otel, prometheus, mlflow, opik, arize, datadog...) and caching (local, redis, redis-semantic, qdrant-semantic, s3, disk) work without Postgres.

LiteLLM gateway-side Anthropic prompt caching is opt-in (LITELLM_ENABLE_ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHING / litellm_settings) with optional 5m/1h TTL; when the client already sends cache_control markers LiteLLM leaves them in place. Claude Code's own cache_control markers (on system blocks and mid-conversation system entries) must be forwarded unchanged and the `system` array must not be reshaped/stringified or the attribution-block strip and caching both break.

When Claude Code is pointed at a gateway with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL plus a credential variable (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN / apiKeyHelper), requests no longer use the claude.ai subscription and are billed per token to the forwarded credential; setting only ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL keeps the subscription login active, but then the gateway must forward the OAuth capability in anthropic-beta to Anthropic.

Claude Code treats an ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway as an Anthropic endpoint and sends the full feature set (adaptive thinking, output_config.effort, context_management, defer_loading/tool_reference, mid-conversation role:system messages, cache_control). A gateway must stream event-by-event (no buffering), forward SSE pings, return retry-after as integer seconds, forward error bodies unmodified, and may optionally expose /v1/models for discovery (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1; only ids containing 'claude' or 'anthropic' are listed). Gateway hint headers (x-claude-code-request-class main|subagent|compaction|auxiliary, x-claude-code-agent-type, x-claude-code-prev-tool-durations, x-claude-code-prompt-id) are sent to a custom base URL only when CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1.

Ollama natively exposes an Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages (messages, streaming, system, tools + tool results, thinking, base64 images, stop_sequences, temperature/top_p/top_k) but NOT tool_choice, metadata or URL images; Claude Code can target it with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="", ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 or `ollama launch claude`; Ollama recommends a 64k+ context window and also offers cloud models (e.g. gemma4:cloud, glm-5.3-flash) through the same local daemon.

Current Anthropic pricing (claude-api skill table cached 2026-10-06, first-party API): claude-opus-5-5 $4/$20 per MTok (cache reads $0.20), claude-sonnet-5-5 $2/$10, claude-haiku-5-5 $0.10/$0.50 (<=100K prompts), claude-haiku-4-5 $1/$5, claude-fable-5-1 $10/$50. Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Fable 5.1 reject disabled thinking and forced tool_choice any/tool, and run the preserved-thinking history-edit check; prefill is removed. The repo's claude-sonnet-4-6 ($3/$15) and claude-opus-4-8 ($5/$25) are older and pricier than their 5.5 successors.

The existing repo router (router/main.py) is a 374-line FastAPI proxy that only speaks /v1/chat/completions, drops `tools`/`tool_choice` entirely (Pydantic ChatCompletionRequest has only model/messages/stream/temperature/max_tokens and Message.content is a str), routes cloud on keyword match or >800 estimated tokens of the last user message only, injects agents.yaml system prompts, and uses stale claude-sonnet-4-6 / claude-opus-4-8 IDs; docker-compose runs ollama + router + open-webui.

Claude Code skills are directories with a SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter + Markdown) loaded in three stages: name+description always in context (combined description/when_to_use capped at 1,536 chars), full body only on invocation, supporting files only when referenced; guidance is to keep SKILL.md under 500 lines; after compaction Claude re-attaches up to 5,000 tokens per invoked skill (25,000 combined). Skill directories are watched, so edits apply within the current session. Frontmatter supports allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, model/effort overrides, context: fork, hooks, and paths globs.

Claude Code skills follow the open Agent Skills standard (agentskills.io, published by Anthropic Dec 2025); Cursor's official docs state each skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md and that Cursor also loads skills from Claude and Codex directories; OpenCode and Codex CLI are also reported to read the format. Portable fields are name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools; Claude-only fields cause validation errors elsewhere.

Anthropic's skill-creator (anthropics/skills, installable as /plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official) implements an eval loop for skills: evals/evals.json (id, prompt, expected_output, files, assertions), each case run twice in isolated subagents with and without the skill (or against an old_skill/ snapshot when improving), a grader subagent writes grading.json (text/passed/evidence per assertion), scripts.aggregate_benchmark produces benchmark.json/.md with pass rate, time and tokens as mean±stddev and delta, an analyzer flags non-discriminating assertions and high-variance (flaky) evals, an optional blind comparator judges two outputs, and scripts.run_loop optimizes the description with a 60/40 train/test split, 3 runs per query, up to 5 iterations.

Claude Code reads a repository's AGENTS.md directly as project instructions when no CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md exists in or above the working directory (requires v2.1.277+); the default setting is claude-md-or-agents-md, and claude-md-and-agents-md loads both. A CLAUDE.md that imports @AGENTS.md remains the portable fallback. CLAUDE.md should target under 200 lines; /doctor prompt-audit (v2.1.283+) audits CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, skills and subagents for conflicts and stale instructions.

Claude Code auto memory is on by default in local sessions, stored machine-locally at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ with a MEMORY.md index plus one topic file per memory, typed as user/feedback/project/reference; only the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md load at session start, topic files load on demand; it can be relocated via autoMemoryDirectory (any settings scope), disabled via autoMemoryEnabled:false or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1; subagents can have their own memory via the subagent memory field; Claude skips facts derivable from the codebase or already in CLAUDE.md.

Claude Code hooks expose 30+ lifecycle events (SessionStart/SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, Stop/StopFailure, PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure, SubagentStart/SubagentStop, TaskCreated/TaskCompleted, PreCompact/PostCompact, PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch, InstructionsLoaded, etc.). Every event receives JSON on stdin with session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, permission_mode; Stop and SubagentStop add last_assistant_message. The transcript file is written asynchronously and may lag the in-memory conversation when a hook fires. Exit 0 = success, exit 2 = block (where blockable), other = non-blocking error. SessionEnd hooks share a 1.5s default budget (raisable to 60s). Hooks live in ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json.

Open WebUI stores thumbs feedback in a Feedback table with fields id, user_id, version, type, data{rating ('1'/'-1' or other), model_id, sibling_model_ids, reason, comment}, meta{arena, chat_id, message_id, tags}, snapshot{chat}, created_at/updated_at, and exposes admin endpoints including GET /feedbacks/all/export (optionally filtered by model_id), GET /feedbacks/list (paginated, order_by, model_id), GET /feedbacks/models, under the evaluations router. Only ratings with a sibling (regenerate or side-by-side/arena) count toward the Elo leaderboard.

GEPA (Genetic-Pareto, gepa-ai/gepa, MIT; paper arXiv:2507.19457) optimizes textual parameters (prompts, code, configs) by having a reflection LM read full execution traces including error messages and textual feedback, maintaining a Pareto frontier of candidates, and mutating/merging them; it needs 100-500 evaluations versus 5,000-25,000+ for GRPO. The optimize() API takes seed_candidate, trainset/valset, task_lm, reflection_lm (required), max_metric_calls, and adapters (DefaultAdapter, DSPy, LangChain). DSPy docs recommend a strong reflection model and describe a cheap task LM + stronger reflection LM as the standard configuration; metrics should return textual feedback, not just a score. Running the reflection LM on Ollama via LiteLLM-style model strings (e.g. ollama_chat/qwen3:8b) is reported in third-party configs but not in official docs.

Kiro (AWS) runs an internal system, kiro-trace, that reads Kiro's own runs to find where it fails or wastes effort, has a model propose a change, and lets deterministic code decide acceptance through a three-stage gate (preselection, regression, confirmation): candidates must also pass tasks Kiro already succeeds at, and the final candidate is compared against an unchanged control on the full benchmark before a normal human code review. In its first week it opened 8 PRs, 7 merged, 1 closed for unrelated reasons, none bounced in review. A documented false positive (a fix that passed more tasks with fewer tokens) was exposed only by splitting results by host: nearly all the gain came from one lucky run escaping a loop. It is not open source.

OpenAI's cookbook 'Build an Agent Improvement Loop with Traces, Evals, and Codex' (May 12, 2026) captures OpenTelemetry-style JSONL traces from agent runs, attaches human SME feedback separately from model critique, converts feedback into Promptfoo evals that can be re-run as a validation gate, uses HALO to rank the next harness changes (harness = instructions, tools, routing, output requirements, validation checks), and writes codex_handoff.md with diagnosis, ranked recommendations and evidence for a coding agent to implement; it recommends starting as a reviewed loop where a developer approves the proposed diff before merge, with deeper automation only once the eval gate is trusted. Default run ~20 minutes for five traces.

ACE (Agentic Context Engineering, Zhang et al., Stanford/SambaNova, arXiv:2510.04618, ICLR 2026) treats the context as an evolving playbook maintained by three roles, Generator, Reflector, Curator, where the Curator emits compact 'delta' items merged into the playbook by lightweight non-LLM logic, explicitly to avoid 'brevity bias' and 'context collapse' from whole-prompt rewrites; reported +10.6% on agent benchmarks and +8.6% on finance. Open implementations exist (sci-m-wang/ACE-open; a PyPI framework released June 2026; kayba-ai agentic-context-engine).

promptfoo is an MIT-licensed CLI/library for LLM evals and red-teaming that runs locally, supports Ollama and 'any LLM API' as providers (so an OpenAI-compatible router endpoint works), is designed for CI/CD regression gates (promptfoo eval / GitHub Action), and is now part of OpenAI while remaining open source. Comparison write-ups consistently position promptfoo as the config-driven prompt-regression gate and Inspect AI as the research-grade benchmark builder (datasets/solvers/scorers/sandboxes), not a PR gate.

Harbor (harbor-framework/harbor) is the official harness for Terminal-Bench 2.0 (harbor run --dataset terminal-bench@2.0), runs tasks in local Docker by default, calls models through LiteLLM provider/model strings, can run agents such as Claude Code, OpenHands and Codex CLI, and exposes third-party datasets (SWE-Bench, Aider Polyglot) via harbor datasets list; task subsets are selectable with -l/--n-tasks and -t/--task-name globs, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints are passed with --ae OPENAI_BASE_URL=... (also OPENAI_API_BASE for LiteLLM-based agents). A smoke test is harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2 -a oracle -l 5.

On a 12GB RTX 3060 the consensus in 2026 guides is a fully-resident 7-8B coder (Qwen2.5-Coder 7B / Qwen3 8B class) at interactive speed, or a 14B at Q4 (~8GB weights) with tight context; Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B at Q4 (~18GB) does not fit in VRAM. No benchmark-backed October-2026 ranking for this card was found.

The repo as of 2026-10-24 has no trace capture or feedback path, duplicates each department system prompt in router/agents.yaml and config/ollama/Modelfile.*, routes local-vs-cloud with keyword lists plus a len(text)//4 token estimate (classify_complexity in router/main.py), references cloud_model claude-sonnet-4-6 (stale), and uses AGENTS.md '[Lessons Learned]' as its only memory, while docs/DESIGN.md plans a custom RAG sidecar, episodic log and lesson-salvaging context pruner that were never built.

Langfuse v4's official docker-compose stack is six services (langfuse-web:4, langfuse-worker:4, ClickHouse 25.12, Postgres 17, Redis 7, MinIO) and the docs recommend at least 4 cores and 16 GiB RAM for the VM; the scaling page's per-component minimums are web 2 CPU/4 GiB, worker 2 CPU/4 GiB, Postgres 2 CPU/4 GiB, Redis 1 CPU/1.5 GiB, ClickHouse 2 CPU/8 GiB (16 GiB for larger), MinIO 2 CPU/4 GiB.

Arize Phoenix runs as a single container (`docker run -p 6006:6006 -p 4317:4317 arizephoenix/phoenix:latest`), defaults to file-based SQLite (set PHOENIX_WORKING_DIR to a volume), accepts OTLP traces on 6006 (/v1/traces HTTP) and 4317 (gRPC), optionally uses Postgres via PHOENIX_SQL_DATABASE_URL, and is free to self-host with 'no license fees, no usage limits, no feature gates' under Elastic License 2.0.

LiteLLM Proxy exposes Prometheus metrics with `litellm_settings: callbacks: ["prometheus"]`; spend metric `litellm_spend_metric` and token metrics `litellm_input_tokens_metric`/`litellm_output_tokens_metric`/`litellm_total_tokens_metric` carry labels end_user, hashed_api_key, api_key_alias, model, team, team_alias, user, requested_model, api_provider; latency histograms `litellm_request_total_latency_metric`, `litellm_llm_api_latency_metric`, `litellm_llm_api_time_to_first_token_metric`. The current docs page carries no enterprise/license notice except for 'Managed Batch Metrics ... Enterprise only'.

LiteLLM lets you override per-token cost per model via `model_info: input_cost_per_token / output_cost_per_token`, and explicitly documents setting both to 0 for Ollama models (`model: ollama/llama3`, `api_base: http://localhost:11434`) so budgets skip them; `cost_per_second` (v1.105.0+) is also available.

Claude Code exports OpenTelemetry metrics when CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 with OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER (otlp|prometheus|console) and OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER; metrics include claude_code.cost.usage (USD; attributes model, query_source, speed, effort, agent.name, skill.name, plugin.name, mcp_server.name, mcp_tool.name), claude_code.token.usage (type input/output/cacheRead/cacheCreation), claude_code.session.count, lines_of_code.count, commit.count, pull_request.count, active_time.total; events include api_request (cost_usd 'Estimated cost in USD', duration_ms, token fields), tool_result, tool_decision, api_error. Default export intervals 60 s metrics / 5 s logs; cardinality flags OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID (true) etc. Tracing (spans) is beta behind CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1.

Claude Code's dollar figures (/usage, status line, OTel cost.usage) are computed locally from token counts at list price and are estimates; 'Claude Max and Pro subscribers have usage included in their subscription, so the session cost figure isn't relevant for billing purposes'. Authoritative billing is only in the Console Usage page. Across enterprise deployments the average is ~$13/developer/active day and $150-250/developer/month at API rates.

Current Anthropic API list prices (per MTok, input/output, cache write/cache read): Fable 5.1 $10/$50, $12.50/$0.25; Opus 5.5 $4/$20, $5/$0.20; Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, $2.50/$0.10; Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50, $0.125/$0.01 (prompts <=100K; $0.50/$2.50 above). Ollama has no native Prometheus/OTel metrics endpoint; tokens/sec must be computed from the final /api/generate or /api/chat response fields (eval_count / eval_duration * 1e9, durations in nanoseconds; also prompt_eval_count, prompt_eval_duration, load_duration, total_duration), and loaded-model VRAM from /api/ps (size_vram, expires_at). The OpenAI-compatible endpoint supports stream_options.include_usage but drops the timing fields. Third-party sidecar exporters exist (e.g. evandhoffman/ollama-prometheus-exporter).

NVIDIA dcgm-exporter targets datacenter Linux/Kubernetes (Docker Desktop 4.37.1+ required for the container), profiling DCGM_FI_PROF_* fields return zero on Ampere, and no source confirms DCGM support under WSL2 or on GeForce.

Anthropic's Usage and Cost Admin API (/v1/organizations/usage_report/messages, /v1/organizations/cost_report) requires an Admin API key and 'is unavailable for individual accounts'; the Cost API is daily-granularity only. Anthropic's SDKs and the API can also emit OpenTelemetry gen_ai.* spans (beta): SDK tracing in-process, and server-side 'API tracing' destinations added via Console/Admin API; Anthropic publishes anthropics/claude-code-monitoring-guide, a compose of otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib (:4317/:4318/:8889), prom/prometheus (:9090) and grafana/grafana (:3000) with provisioned dashboards.

The repo's current router (router/main.py) returns estimated token counts for Ollama (estimate_tokens on the text) and only input_tokens from Anthropic, emits no structured per-request usage/latency log, and the README still references claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-opus-4-8, which are superseded by Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 at lower prices.

Ollama now serves every GGUF model by spawning the upstream llama.cpp `llama-server` binary as a subprocess (its own Go runner is no longer used for GGUF). Consequently Ollama inherits llama-server's auto layer fitting, flash-attention 'auto', KV-cache quantization and speculative decoding, and there is no raw-throughput reason to replace Ollama with a hand-run llama-server for dense models.

On a 12 GB card Ollama's default context window is 4096 tokens: the server picks 4096 when total VRAM < 23 GiB, 32768 for 23-47 GiB, 262144 for >=47 GiB, unless OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH or a per-request/Modelfile num_ctx overrides it. Ollama's own docs say agentic/coding workloads should use at least 64k. Leaving the default means tool-call histories get truncated silently.

Ollama env-var defaults (source of truth, main branch Oct 2026): OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1, OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=0 (auto -> 3 per GPU), OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE=512, OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=5m (negative = infinite, 0 = unload immediately), OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=f16, OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION unset (tri-state: unset -> 'auto'), OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=0 (VRAM-tiered), OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD=0 bytes, OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD disables cloud features, OLLAMA_REMOTES default 'ollama.com'.

Flash attention: when OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION is unset Ollama passes `--flash-attn auto` to llama-server on supported GPUs (so it is effectively on for Qwen3/gpt-oss/Gemma on an RTX 3060); OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 forces `--flash-attn on`, =0 forces off. KV-cache quantization (OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0/q4_0) is passed as `--cache-type-k/--cache-type-v`, applies globally to all models, and per Ollama's FAQ only takes effect with flash attention; q8_0 ~ half of f16 with negligible quality loss, q4_0 ~ quarter with small-to-medium loss that grows with context and with high-GQA models.

Same-model concurrency: Ollama launches llama-server with `-c num_ctx*num_parallel -np num_parallel` and wraps it in an in-process weighted semaphore of size num_parallel. With the default NUM_PARALLEL=1, a second simultaneous request to the same model blocks on the semaphore until the first completes (no error, honours client cancellation); setting NUM_PARALLEL=2 doubles the KV allocation (each slot gets a full num_ctx) in exchange for batched decoding. Overflow beyond OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE pending requests returns HTTP 503 'server busy, please try again. maximum pending requests exceeded'.

Different-model concurrency: when a request arrives for a model that is not loaded, the scheduler predicts its VRAM (weights + KV for num_ctx*num_parallel + batch buffers); if the prediction exceeds 80% of currently free memory it evicts another runner, choosing an idle one (refCount==0) sorted by soonest expiry/name, and if none is idle it waits for the in-flight request to finish and then unloads. On a 12 GB card this means two agents using two different ~9 GB models alternately will reload each switch (seconds each) rather than run together; only pairs whose combined footprint fits (e.g., a 14B Q4 + a <1 GiB embedding model) are co-resident.

Ollama keys loaded runners by the GGUF blob path (ModelPath), not by model name. Six Modelfile-derived agent models (`FROM qwen3:14b` + SYSTEM) therefore share one loaded runner and cost no extra VRAM, PROVIDED their PARAMETER values (num_ctx, num_batch, etc.) are identical; a differing num_ctx triggers `needsReload` and a full reload on every agent switch. A `system` message supplied in the API request is rendered into the template for that request and takes precedence over the Modelfile SYSTEM.

Ollama does NOT pass a MoE expert-offload flag (`--n-cpu-moe` / `--cpu-moe` / `-ot`) to llama-server; its only load-mode controls are `--load-mode none|dio` (mmap) and whatever `-ngl` auto-fit llama-server does itself. For an MoE model larger than VRAM (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, 18.6 GB Q4_K_M) Ollama therefore offloads whole layers (attention included) to CPU, which is markedly slower than llama-server's expert-only offload.

Windows: the official Ollama Windows install is a native app (no admin, user-profile install, API on localhost:11434, NVIDIA driver >= 551.61, env vars set as USER environment variables then quit tray app and relaunch; models in %HOMEPATH%\.ollama, relocatable via OLLAMA_MODELS; logs in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\server.log). The Ollama Docker image supports GPU on Windows only via Docker Desktop's WSL2 backend plus nvidia-container-toolkit; Ollama's docker/gpu docs give no Windows-specific guidance. Community guides consistently recommend native Windows for a single-GPU desktop and report WSL2/Docker-specific failure modes (GPU vanishing after driver updates, need for `wsl --shutdown`, WSL VM restart loops when a GPU model loads at boot, port 11434 conflicts when both are installed).

KV-cache cost per token (K+V, all layers) derived from architecture: Qwen3-14B (40 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128) = 160 KiB f16 / 80 KiB q8_0 / 40 KiB q4_0 -> 16k ctx: 2.5 / 1.25 / 0.63 GiB; 32k: 5.0 / 2.5 / 1.25 GiB. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (48 layers, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128) = 96 KiB f16 / 48 KiB q8_0 -> 16k: 1.5 / 0.75 GiB; 32k: 3.0 / 1.5 GiB; 64k: 6.0 / 3.0 GiB. gpt-oss-20b (24 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 64, alternating 128-token sliding-window and full layers) = 48 KiB f16 if every layer kept full context, but with llama.cpp's SWA-aware cache only the 12 full layers scale, ~24 KiB f16 / 12 KiB q8_0 -> 32k: ~0.75 / ~0.4 GiB (1.5 GiB f16 if --swa-full). Formula: 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * bytes.

Weight footprints: Qwen3-14B Q4_K_M = 8.38-9.00 GB depending on quantizer; Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct Q4_K_M = 18.6 GB; gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 is '21B parameters with 3.6B active', 'runs within 16GB of memory', GGUF roughly 12-13 GB (exact size unverified). On an RTX 3060 12 GB with Windows WDDM holding ~0.5-1 GiB, usable VRAM is roughly 10.5-11 GiB, so: Qwen3-14B Q4_K_M + 16k q8_0 KV + ~0.5 GiB compute buffers ~= 10.3 GiB FITS (tight; use OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD or a Q4_K_S quant for margin); 32k does NOT fit without q4_0 KV; Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B cannot fit its weights at any useful quant and must use expert CPU offload (requires system RAM >= ~20 GB free, i.e. a 32-64 GB machine); gpt-oss-20b spills ~1-2 GB to CPU under Ollama with estimated low-to-mid-teens tok/s.

The current MCP specification revision is 2026-07-28; it removes the initialize/initialized handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header, requires Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers on Streamable HTTP POST requests, adds a server/discover RPC that servers must implement, and carries protocol version and client capabilities in _meta on every request.

In 2026-07-28, Roots, Sampling and Logging are deprecated with a minimum twelve-month support window; the legacy HTTP+SSE transport is formally deprecated; OAuth Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents but 'continues to work for backward compatibility'; Tasks move from core into the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension using poll-based tasks/get and tasks/update.

The 2026-07-28 spec recommends that servers needing cross-call state mint an explicit handle from a tool and have the model pass it back as an argument; all four Tier-1 SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Go, C#) support 2026-07-28 at release, Rust in beta.

The official MCP Registry (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) is still a preview with the API frozen at v0.1 and GA undated; it verifies only namespace ownership (GitHub OAuth/OIDC, DNS or HTTP proof) and performs no code or security vetting; entries grew from ~17k (Jul 2026) to ~30k (Sep 2026) to ~45k names (Oct 2026).

Only seven reference servers remain maintained in modelcontextprotocol/servers (everything, fetch, filesystem, git, memory, sequential-thinking, time); GitHub, GitLab, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Puppeteer, Brave Search, Slack, Redis, Google Drive/Maps, Sentry, AWS KB and EverArt are archived. Current versions: @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem, server-memory and server-sequential-thinking 2.0.0 (2026-10-19, Node 24+ required); mcp-server-git 2026.10.19 on PyPI.

The filesystem reference server scopes access by positional allowed-directory arguments ('the only method that works on every protocol version'); MCP Roots are deprecated and unusable on 2026-07-28 connections; there is no global read-only flag, read-only is achieved per Docker bind mount with ',ro' and write_file refuses read-only files.

GitHub's official MCP server runs remotely at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ (OAuth or PAT as Bearer) or locally via ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server; tool exposure is controlled with --toolsets / GITHUB_TOOLSETS ('default' = context, repos, issues, pull_requests, users; 20+ toolsets incl. actions, code_security, dependabot, secret_protection), --tools for individual tools, and --read-only which 'skips write tools even if requested'.

Playwright MCP (@playwright/mcp, 0.0.83 published 2026-09-28) runs via npx @playwright/mcp@latest; default mode uses accessibility snapshots (no screenshots), --caps=vision opts into coordinate tools; --headless, --isolated, --allowed-origins/--blocked-origins ('does not serve as a security boundary'), --output-dir and --port N expose Streamable HTTP at http://localhost:N/mcp.

Serena (serena-agent 2.1.0 on PyPI, 2026-10-19; MIT) provides LSP-backed symbol tools for 40+ languages; it is started with `serena start-mcp-server` with --context (desktop-app default; claude-code 'disables tools that would duplicate Claude Code's built-in capabilities'; codex; ide; agent/oaicompat-agent), --mode (planning, editing, interactive, one-shot, no-onboarding, no-memories, ...), --project / --project-from-cwd, --transport stdio|streamable-http|sse (sse discouraged) and --port; it is stateful with one active project, so one streamable-http instance should be shared only by clients on the same project.

Serena's read_only project setting and tool exclusions are 'not a security mechanism': editing tools are refused but REPL-submitted code can still modify files; project trust is keyed on trusted_project_path_patterns (v1.6.0+) and is 'a functionality boundary, not a containment boundary'; the recommended hard sandbox is running Serena in Docker exposing only necessary files.

Claude Code MCP config: three scopes (local in ~/.claude.json, project in ./.mcp.json shared via git, user in ~/.claude.json) with precedence local > project > user > plugin > claude.ai connectors and no field merging; .mcp.json uses an `mcpServers` object where `type` is stdio | http (alias streamable-http) | sse (deprecated) | ws, stdio entries have command/args/env, remote entries url/headers/headersHelper, optional per-server `timeout` ms and `alwaysLoad`; `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` expand in command/args/env/url/headers, but credential-like names (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, HTTPS_PROXY...) read as empty in url/headers; project .mcp.json servers require interactive approval (reset with `claude mcp reset-project-choices`).

Claude Code tool search is on by default (MCP tool definitions deferred; only names and server instructions load at start) on Opus 4/Sonnet 4/Haiku 4.5 and later; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false|auto|auto:N controls it; `alwaysLoad: true` on a server loads its tools upfront and makes startup wait up to the 5 s connect timeout; MCP output warns at 10,000 tokens, defaults to a 25,000-token cap (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS), persists results over 50,000 chars to a file (raise per tool via _meta['anthropic/maxResultSizeChars'] up to 500k); tool names over 128 chars are dropped; tool descriptions loaded via search may be up to 16,384 chars.

OpenCode configures MCP in its config (opencode.json with "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json") under a top-level `mcp` map: local servers use type "local", `command` as an array, optional `cwd`, `environment`, `enabled`, `timeout` (ms, default 30000 'when connecting and fetching tools'); remote servers use type "remote", `url`, `headers`, `oauth` ({clientId, clientSecret, scope} or false), with `opencode mcp auth|list|logout|debug` and tokens in ~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json; tools are named <server>_<tool> and can be disabled globally with `tools: {"server_*": false}` then re-enabled per agent; docs warn each server adds context and the GitHub server can exceed the context limit.

Open WebUI has native MCP support since v0.6.31 (2025-09-25) but only for Streamable HTTP ('Native MCP support in Open WebUI is Streamable HTTP only'); servers are added by admins at Settings > Admin > Integrations > External Tool Servers with Type 'MCP (Streamable HTTP)' and auth None/Bearer/Session/OAuth/OAuth 2.1 (DCR or static); WEBUI_SECRET_KEY must be set or OAuth tokens fail to decrypt after restart; users enable tools per chat via + > Integrations > Tools, admins can set non-OAuth tools as model defaults, tools appear to the model as <server ID>_<tool name> (64-char limit), Tool Search can defer definitions, and OpenAPI 'remains the preferred integration path' for most deployments. stdio/SSE servers still require mcpo (mcpo 0.0.20, last PyPI release 2026-02-27).

A2A is a Linux Foundation project (Apache 2.0, contributed by Google) that reached v1.0.0 on 2026-03-12 (breaking changes, tasks/list, gRPC multi-tenancy, spec split into protocol + transport mappings) and v1.0.1 on 2026-05-28; signed Agent Cards and mTLS arrived in v0.3.0 (2025-07-30); it uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP(S) with SSE streaming and push notifications and is positioned as complementary to MCP (agents collaborating vs. agents using tools); 150+ supporting organizations as of April 2026.

Exposing an orchestrator/agent as an MCP server with a delegate-style tool is an established pattern (Microsoft Agent Framework 'agents as MCP tools' with one tool per operation or a single ask-anything entry point; sub-agents-mcp run_agent backed by claude/cursor CLIs; SubMCP delegate_parallel with read-only sandboxed sub-agents by default), with the recognised caveat that MCP tool calls are synchronous request/response so long delegations need async handling.

OWASP's recommended 'Client-Side Tool Risk Gating' control: record a SHA-256 fingerprint of each tool's canonical definition (name, description, input schema) on first sight, recompute on every reconnect, and move any changed tool to AWAITING_REREVIEW 'withheld from re-exposure until a human explicitly re-approves it' so 'a rug-pull redefinition therefore cannot ride in on a prior approval'; classify tools L0-L5 from readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint with floors for destructive verbs (delete_, drop_, purge_, wipe_) and missing metadata raising risk; gate designated tools behind per-invocation human approval; enforce a deny-by-default ceiling so 'the model never sees a tool above the ceiling'; explicit registration only, no silent auto-discovery; it does not inspect tool results, so injection via retrieved content is 'bounded, not detected'.

The repository's shipped Continue config (config/vscode/continue.config.json) hardcodes the stale cloud model IDs claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-opus-4-8 in both model entries and descriptions, and points every department at the router's OpenAI-compatible endpoint without any MCP server configuration.
